newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London easier, await Wall Street lead.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London easier, await Wall Street lead.

text.p: U.S. shares were slightly lower in quiet trade on Wednesday with most European investors content to stay on the sidelines after the Dow's record close Tuesday.
Dealers noted that the broader based high-tech laden Nasdaq Composite index finished lower on Tuesday -- continuing to underperform blue chips.
"The Dow barely squeezed out a record yesterday and Nasdaq fell back. The divergence between the second-liners and the Dow is getting wider," one market maker said.
"Some people fear the second-liners are pointing to the future--down."
Since January 22, when the Nasdaq Composite closed at a record level of 1,388.06, the Dow has risen 235.13 points, or 3.4 percent, hitting a new high of 7.085.16 on Tuesday.
But during the same period, the Nasdaq has dropped 71.3 points or 5.19 percent.
Cisco Systems, which dropped $5/8 to $52-3/4 on Tuesday was up $1/8 to $52-7/8 but trading volume was thin.
"We've seen a little bit of bottom fishing in the stock but nothing convincing," one dealer said. Cisco shares have slumped $23 or 30 percent since January 24.
The June T-bond was down 6/32 to 109-26/32 by 1205 GMT. The yield on the 30-year cash long bond was standing at 6.85 percent.
